findings.text: Kept as an advisory (Q2). RECEIVED_VISIBLE now gives the same answer as boundAliasesOf: it joins a.alias = l.bound_alias and ties l.bound_alias = x.remote_alias. Its EXISTS still restates the binding conditions of levels.ts:82-85 in its own SQL, because a function cannot be called inside the query. This is a maintenance risk, not a wrong result.

Kept as an advisory (Q8). I confirmed that validate.ts:37 re-exports parseEntryUid and that no production caller imports it from there. Note: test-quality's upheld F-3 asks that team-validate.test.ts import it from validate.ts again, as the base did. That would make this re-export used, so this finding should not be fixed by deleting it.
Kept as an advisory (Q8). ENTRY_UID is exported, but only parseEntryUid in the same file reads it. An unused export is a cosmetic matter.

Kept as an advisory (Q5). Now that ReceivedScope has one field, receivedScope only wraps its argument, and two other callers build the same object inline. This is a thin layer, with no effect on behaviour.

Upheld as a defect (Q3), as in round 4. Nothing has changed since: AC-85 (preserve) is still live in probes/criteria.md:13 with the same text. It allows only the two configured-server sentences of this file to change. The diff (diff.patch:6984-7102) also changes the saveSettings call and the two signature regexes, and it adds the Servers card cases, the dock case and the last-change assertions. So AC-85's 'passes unchanged' is false for this file. The gate cannot waive a live criterion. The person has to retire or restate AC-85.

Upheld as a defect (Q4, the claim of an observed criterion is false). I checked diff.patch:7012-7016: three assertions (muted, unmuted, '"removed" : "added"') are added to the existing case 'says how many projects share, and the last change'. AC-92 (probes/criteria.md:19) lists the changes this file may have: the two configured-server sentences, the saveSettings call, the two signature regexes, the Servers card's cases and the dock's Receive only case. It does not name the last-change case, so its 'everything else … passes unchanged' is false here. Either AC-92 is restated to name this case, or the assertions move into a new case the criterion covers.

Upheld as a defect (Q4, the claim of an observed criterion is false). diff.patch:6969-6976 changes this server test's import so that it takes parseEntryUid from src/team/contract.ts. AC-91 (probes/criteria.md:18) says tests/unit/team-*.test.ts 'pass unchanged on the final tree'. I confirmed that src/team/validate.ts:37 still re-exports parseEntryUid (`export { entryBytes, parseEntryUid };`), so the base's import would still resolve and pass. Restoring the base's import lines makes AC-91 true again.

Kept as an advisory (Q5). The case matches the template source instead of running serverChange on the values muteServer logs. It does fail when the round 4 code comes back, but it would not catch the old and new values being swapped. The rubric files an implementation-coupled test that still fails on reversion as an advisory.

Kept as an advisory (Q5). basis-full and sm:basis-auto are looked for anywhere in Servers.vue, not on the action group itself. The not.toContain('flex-none flex-wrap') check fails on reversion, and the 360 captures are the visual proof.

Kept as an advisory (public-api). This is unchanged from round 4. Pull-page items get no shape check where they enter, and the answer body has no size cap. Path components are checked, entry uids go through the strict parseEntryUid, and an item that throws is set aside.

Kept as an advisory (personal-data). This is unchanged. A received memory is filed under any enabled project that holds the alias, with no aliasBoundTo check. The brief and the prompt keep the row out, and only the receiving member can see it.

Kept as an advisory (personal-data). This is unchanged. Received memories become ordinary rows, and memory_search and the consolidation neighbours, which this diff did not write, apply no mute or binding check. That is debt.
Kept as an advisory (personal-data). This is unchanged. After a restore, deleting the copies of an unlisted server waits for a manual sync --once, and the CLI tells the person so.
Kept as an advisory (auth). This is unchanged. --code on argv shows the invitation code in shell history and ps. A no-echo prompt exists, and the usage text names it.
Kept as an advisory (auth). This is unchanged. Remove forgets the token only on this machine. The person is told that the device stays valid until an admin revokes it.
Kept as an advisory (auth). This is unchanged. The resume and add confirmations act on the state at that moment, not on the preview the person saw. Nothing beyond the policy is sent.

Kept as an advisory. The held state is declared and captured (review/ui/settings-held@768-dark.png, review/ui/settings-held@360-light.png). Only holdLine's branch with n withdrawals has no capture, and that branch is not a declared state the manifest lists as missing. Round 4 ruled the same.
Kept as an advisory. Stale toasts stack across the states (review/ui/settings-listed@360-dark.png). They cover no control any state needs. Round 4 ruled the same.

Kept as an advisory. The reviewer files this as cosmetic: Remove… and Rejoin… open a plain modal, while Resume… opens one with an icon tile. Both read clearly (review/ui/settings-removing@360-dark.png, review/ui/settings-resuming@360-light.png).

Kept as an advisory (Q1/Q4). This is unchanged since round 4. The 'held pull answered at once' rule measures the time since the last answer, so the back-off does not double as spec.md:187 says. The server's hold limits the loop, and status shows the last error.
Kept as an advisory (Q1). This is unchanged. INDEXED BY sharing_memories_updated fails on a store that lacks the index. ADR 0027:87 limits this to unreleased development stores.

Kept as an advisory (Q1). This is carried unchanged from round 2. The sync runs its own SQL over the knowledge module's tables, and no boundary test guards it. The base draws no explicit rule that this breaks.
Kept as an advisory (Q3). This is carried unchanged from round 2. RESULT_SHAPES.refusal leaves out the optional accepted and retryAfterSec keys that RefusalShape declares and the client reads.
